words.ex: We achieved our export target this quarter.
use: She achieved great results in the new market.
그녀는 새 시장에서 좋은 성과를 냈다.
What do you want to achieve this year?
mcq: He achieved a 20% increase in sales.
He achieved in the sales target.
words.note: achieve + 명사(목표·성과). achieve to는 쓰지 않아요.

words.ex: I built my career in overseas sales.
use: This project was a turning point in my career.
She started her career as an intern.
mcq: I've spent my career in cosmetics.
My career works in sales field.
words.note: career는 직업명이 아니라 '경력의 흐름'. My job is~ 와 구분!

words.ex: Our goal is to enter the US market.
use: We set clear goals for each quarter.
The team reached its sales goal early.
mcq: We set a goal for next year.
We made a goal for next year.
We built a goal for next year.
We put a goal to next year.
words.note: set a goal이 정확한 짝(collocation)이에요.

words.ex: Feel free to contact me anytime.
use: I'll contact the buyer this week.
mcq: Please contact to me by email.
Please contact with me by email.
Please contact for me by email.
words.note: contact + 사람 바로! contact to/with는 한국식 오류의 대표주자.

words.ex: I regard him as a mentor.
use: She is regarded as an expert in K-beauty.
Please give my regards to your team.
mcq: I regard him as a good partner.
I regard him a good partner.
I regard him to a good partner.
I regard him being good partner.
words.note: regard A as B. as를 빼먹기 쉬워요! 이메일 끝 Best regards도 이 단어.

words.ex: I have 10 years of experience in sales.
use: We experienced some delays in shipping.
mcq: I have many experiences of sales.
I have a lot of experience in sales.
I have much experience about sales.
words.note: 경력의 experience는 셀 수 없는 명사! experience in + 분야.

words.ex: Please inform us of any changes.
use: I'll inform the client about the delay.
We were informed that the meeting was canceled.
mcq: I informed the schedule to him.
I informed him of the schedule.
I informed to him the schedule.
I informed about him the schedule.
words.note: inform + 사람 + of/about + 내용. 사람이 먼저 와요!

words.ex: Let's examine the contract carefully.
use: The team examined the market data.
words.note: examine + 대상 바로 연결. review보다 더 꼼꼼히 보는 느낌이에요.

words.ex: We received some negative feedback.
use: Don't be so negative about the plan.
words.note: be + negative(형용사). 검사 결과 '음성'도 negative예요.

words.ex: They're our biggest business partner.
use: We partnered with a local distributor.
Finding the right partner takes time.
맞는 파트너를 찾는 데는 시간이 걸린다.
mcq: We partnered with a Chinese company.
We partnered to a Chinese company.
We partnered a company together with.
words.note: partner with + 회사 = ~와 제휴하다. 동사로도 써요!

words.ex: What's the procedure for customs clearance?
use: The visa procedure takes two weeks.
mcq: Follow the safety process of procedure.
words.note: procedure(절차) vs process(과정) vs proceed(진행하다) — 셋을 구분!

words.ex: We conducted a customer survey.
use: The company conducts market research every year.
The interview was conducted in English.
mcq: We conducted a meeting with the buyer.
words.note: conduct + 조사/회의/실험. do보다 격식 있는 비즈니스 동사!

words.ex: Speak with confidence in the meeting.
use: I have confidence in our product.
The buyer lost confidence in the supplier.
바이어가 그 공급사에 대한 신뢰를 잃었다.
mcq: I have confidence in this plan.
I have confidence to this plan.
I have confidence about this plan well.
I am confidence in this plan.
words.note: confidence in + 대상. 형용사는 confident (I am confident)!

words.ex: You need a permit to sell here.
use: The law doesn't permit this kind of ad.
Weather permitting, we'll visit the factory.
mcq: Smoking is not permit in here.
words.note: be permitted = 허용되다. allow의 격식 버전이에요.

words.ex: This app works on any device.
use: Please turn off all electronic devices.
mcq: I bought a new device for testing.
I bought a new device machine.
I bought a machinery device tool.
words.note: device 하나면 충분! 비슷한 말을 겹쳐 쓰지 않아요.

words.ex: It's been a long journey to this success.
use: The journey from Seoul to Paris takes 14 hours.
Learning English is a journey, not a race.
words.note: journey는 긴 이동·여정. trip(짧은 여행)과 겹쳐 쓰지 않기!

words.ex: They rejected our first offer.
use: The buyer rejected the samples due to quality.
words.note: reject + 대상 바로 연결. refuse보다 공식적인 거절 느낌.

words.ex: Have faith in yourself.
use: I have faith in this team.
mcq: I have faith in our new product.
I have faith to our new product.
I have faith about our product.
I am faith in our product.
words.note: faith in + 대상. 비즈니스에서 in good faith(선의로)도 자주 나와요.

words.ex: There's a big gap between the two prices.
use: We need to close the gap with competitors.
There's a gap in the market for men's skincare.
mcq: There's a gap between price and quality.
There's a gap among price and quality.
There's a gap of between prices.
The gap is between to prices.
words.note: gap between A and B. 둘 사이는 between!

words.ex: Don't let emotions drive your decisions.
use: Her voice was full of emotion.
Good ads connect with customers' emotions.
words.note: emotion(명사) vs emotional(형용사) 구분이 포인트!

words.ex: Don't be afraid of making mistakes.
use: I made a mistake in the report.
words.note: make a mistake! do가 아니라 make — 최고 빈출 짝(collocation)이에요.

words.ex: There's a schedule conflict on Friday.
use: The meeting conflicts with my class.
mcq: The two meetings conflict with each other.
The two meetings conflict to each other.
words.note: conflict with = ~와 겹치다/충돌하다. 일정 얘기할 때 아주 유용!

words.ex: Does your insurance cover this?
use: I need travel insurance for the trip.
mcq: I bought one insurance of travel.
words.note: insurance는 셀 수 없는 명사! a를 붙이지 않아요.

words.ex: She works in finance.
mcq: The bank financed the new building.
The bank financed to the building.
The bank made finance the building.
words.note: finance는 동사로 '자금을 대다'로도 써요.

words.ex: I can't concentrate with this noise.
words.exko: 이 소음 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
use: Let's concentrate on the main issue.
She concentrated hard on the test.
words.note: concentrate on! focus on과 같은 전치사예요.

words.ex: I'll definitely be there!
use: This is definitely the best option.
mcq: I will definitely to call you.
I will call definitely be you.
words.note: definitely는 조동사와 본동사 사이! 대답 한마디로도 자주 써요.

words.ex: I trust your judgment.
use: In my judgment, we should wait.
words.note: use one's judgment = 알아서 판단하다. 업무에서 아주 자주 쓰는 표현!

words.ex: Be careful with that glass.
use: She's very careful about spending money.
mcq: Be careful of the wet floor.
words.note: be careful of/with + 대상. carefully는 부사!

words.ex: Excuse me, can I ask you something?
use: Stop making excuses and just do it.
That's no excuse for being late.
mcq: He made an excuse for being late.
He did an excuse for being late.
He took an excuse for late.
He got excuse to being late.
words.note: make an excuse = 변명하다. mistake처럼 make와 짝!

words.ex: Stay calm and think clearly.
use: The sea was calm this morning.
Take a deep breath and calm down.
mcq: Please calm down, everything is fine.
words.note: calm down 그 자체로 '진정하다'. be calm down처럼 섞지 않기!

words.ex: I got a small gift for you.
use: She has a gift for languages.
This watch was a gift from my father.
mcq: He has a gift for music.
He has a gift of doing music at.
He is a gift for music.
words.note: have a gift for = ~에 재능이 있다. '선물' 말고 이 뜻도 기억!

words.ex: The wind is blowing hard today.
use: Losing the deal was a big blow to us.
그 계약을 놓친 건 우리에게 큰 타격이었다.
mcq: The news was a big blow to him.
The news was a big blow at him.
The news blew him a big.
The news was blowing big him.
words.note: a blow to + 대상 = ~에게 타격. 명사 blow도 자주 써요.

words.ex: She's studying abroad in Canada.
mcq: I want to work in abroad.
I want to work to abroad.
I want to work at the abroad.
words.note: abroad 앞에 전치사 금지! 그 자체가 '해외로/에서'예요.

words.ex: I have to admit, you were right.
use: He admitted his mistake right away.
I hate to admit it, but I was wrong.
mcq: I admit to be late yesterday.
He admitted that he forgot the meeting.
She admitted me her secret plan.
words.note: admit + that절 또는 admit + -ing. 'admit to be'는 틀린 형태예요.

words.ex: Can I borrow your pen for a second?
use: I borrowed some money from my brother.
You can borrow up to five books.
책을 다섯 권까지 빌릴 수 있어요.
mcq: Can you borrow me your charger?
She borrowed a pen to me.
words.note: borrow는 '내가 빌려오다'. 남에게 빌려주는 건 lend예요. 'borrow me'는 한국식 오류!

words.ex: The flight was delayed by two hours.
use: Let's not delay the decision any longer.
mcq: The meeting delayed because of him.
The meeting was delayed because of the weather.
We delayed to start the project.
words.note: 주어가 지연되는 쪽이면 be delayed(수동). delay + -ing도 가능하지만 delay to는 안 돼요.

words.ex: I prefer tea to coffee.
use: I'd prefer to stay home tonight.
오늘 밤은 집에 있는 게 더 좋겠어.
words.note: prefer A to B! than이 아니라 to를 쓰는 게 포인트예요.

words.ex: Regular exercise prevents many diseases.
use: The rain prevented us from leaving.
How can we prevent this from happening again?
이런 일이 재발하지 않게 하려면 어떻게 해야 할까?
mcq: The noise prevented me to sleep.
The noise prevented me from sleeping.
The noise prevented that I sleep.
The noise prevented my sleep from.
words.note: prevent + 사람 + from + -ing. 'prevent to'는 한국인이 가장 많이 틀리는 형태!

words.ex: Remind me to call her tomorrow.
use: This song reminds me of my school days.
이 노래를 들으면 학창 시절이 생각나.
I reminded him about the deadline.
mcq: This photo reminds me of our trip.
This photo remembers me our trip.
This photo reminds to me our trip.
I remind this photo of the trip.
words.note: remind A of B = A에게 B를 떠올리게 하다. remember(기억하다)와 혼동 주의!

words.ex: Can you recommend a good restaurant?
use: The doctor recommended getting more sleep.
mcq: I recommend you to this cafe strongly.
words.note: recommend + 명사/-ing가 자연스러워요. 'recommend you to 장소'는 어색합니다.

words.ex: I didn't expect to see you here!
use: We expect the package to arrive tomorrow.
Don't expect too much from the movie.
mcq: I expect that he will come.
He expects me that I go.
words.note: expect + that절 / expect + to부정사. 'expect him coming'은 어색해요.

words.ex: Can I suggest a different plan?
use: I suggest that we take a break.
mcq: I suggest you to go home early.
I suggest to go home early.
words.note: suggest + -ing! 'suggest to go'는 한국인이 가장 많이 틀리는 형태예요.

words.ex: I totally agree with you.
use: We agreed to meet next week.
I don't agree with that idea.
words.note: agree with + 사람/의견. 'I am agree'는 be동사 없이 I agree!

words.ex: What time does the train arrive?
use: We arrived at the hotel around noon.
She arrived in Seoul last night.
words.note: arrive at + 장소(건물), arrive in + 도시/나라. arrive to는 없어요!

words.ex: Will you attend the meeting tomorrow?
use: About fifty people attended the seminar.
I can't attend the wedding this Saturday.
mcq: I will attend to the meeting.
I will attend at the meeting.
I will attend in the meeting.
words.note: attend + 행사 바로 연결! 전치사를 넣는 게 대표적인 실수예요.

words.ex: Please raise your hand if you have a question.
use: Can I raise one more question?
mcq: They raised the price last month.
The price was raise by them.
They rose the price last month.
words.note: raise는 목적어가 필요(올리다). 스스로 오르는 건 rise! rise-rose-risen과 혼동 주의.

words.ex: We finally reached the top of the mountain.
use: You can reach me by email anytime.
mcq: We reached to the station at 9.
We reached at the station at 9.
We reached in the station at 9.
words.note: reach + 장소 바로 연결! arrive at과 헷갈려서 reach to로 쓰기 쉬워요.

words.ex: I'm having trouble with my computer.
use: He got into trouble at school.
mcq: I have trouble to sleep at night.
I have trouble sleeping at night.
I have a trouble for sleeping.
words.note: have trouble + -ing! 'trouble to sleep'이 아니에요.

words.ex: This watch has great sentimental value.
use: The value of the house went up.
mcq: This experience is value to me.
This experience has value to me.
words.note: have value = 가치가 있다. valuable(형용사)과 구분하세요.

words.ex: This is my second attempt at the test.
use: He attempted to fix it himself.
mcq: I attempted that I solve it.
words.note: attempt + to부정사. try보다 격식 있는 말이에요.

words.ex: Please let me know in advance.
use: Technology advances so fast these days.
Thank you in advance for your help.
words.note: in advance = 미리. 전치사 in이 고정이에요.

words.ex: The company has about 200 employees.
mcq: I am an employee at a bank.
I am an employer at a bank as staff.
I work as an employer for my boss.
words.note: employee = 고용된 직원, employer = 고용주(회사). -ee가 '받는 쪽'!

words.ex: I try to exercise three times a week.
words.note: do exercise 또는 그냥 exercise(동사). play는 구기 종목에만!

words.ex: Push the door, don't pull it.
use: Don't push me, I need time.
She pushed herself to finish the race.
mcq: He pushed me to try again.
He pushed that I try again.
He pushed to me for trying.
words.note: push + 사람 + to부정사 = ~하도록 밀어붙이다.

words.ex: Your English is improving fast!
use: I want to improve my speaking skills.
The weather improved in the afternoon.
words.note: improve 하나로 충분해요. improve up 같은 군더더기 불필요!

words.ex: The hotel provides free breakfast.
use: We provide customers with fast service.
The company provided lunch for everyone.
mcq: They provide us with good service.
They provide to us good service.
They provide good service for we.
words.note: provide A with B = A에게 B를 제공하다. with를 빼먹기 쉬워요!

words.ex: I love fruit, especially strawberries.
use: The hotel is busy, especially on weekends.
mcq: I like summer, specially August season.
Especially, I like the August most.
words.note: especially는 예시 앞에 붙어요. specially(특별히 맞춤으로)와 구분!

words.ex: We went out despite the rain.
use: Despite the price, the room was small.
mcq: Despite of the rain, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
Despite it rained, we went out.
Despite for the rain, we went out.
words.note: despite + 명사 바로 연결! 'despite of'는 정말 흔한 오류예요(in spite of와 혼동).

words.ex: The buffet has a variety of dishes.
use: We offer a variety of room types.
I eat a variety of vegetables.
mcq: They sell a variety of drinks.
words.note: a variety of + 복수명사. 관사 a를 빼먹기 쉬워요!

words.ex: I'm preparing for a job interview.
use: She prepared dinner for the guests.
We need to prepare for the busy season.
words.note: prepare for + 대비할 일. prepare + 명사(직접 만들 것)도 가능해요.
